1	# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya
2	
3	> Status: draft v3, for owner review · Updated: 2026-11-09
4	> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
5	> what it gives Compliance.
6	
7	## How to read this
8	
9	Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
10	Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
11	auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.
12	
13	| Marker | Meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes or links the official page (one row, R2.4.1b, is an AWS blog). |
16	| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5), or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row. Reasoned, not documented. |
17	| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
18	| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |
19	
20	Nothing here was checked locally (✅): this is a design without access to Papaya's systems.
21	**GĐ-n** = assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4 (owner-confirmed: GĐ-1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11,
22	14; the others are marked "unconfirmed" where used); **S-n** = success criteria
23	(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
24	`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **OD-n** = owner decisions on this draft (both at the end).
25	Earlier owner answers are cited with their source: "research 6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options §9 Q2".
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. The decision in one page
30	
31	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
32	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
33	
34	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
35	
36	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
37	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
38	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
39	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
40	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
41	
42	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
43	|---|---|
44	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
45	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, OD1, OD6; storage conditions [design], layer 5). |
46	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
47	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
48	
49	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
50	
51	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
52	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
53	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
54	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
55	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
56	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an owner of the stack approves the prod preview [design].
57	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
58	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
59	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
60	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
61	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
62	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
63	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
64	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** code-owner review means an approver must own the file,
65	  at L2 as at L3. So that one on-call primary can approve any path at 2 a.m., the on-call approver
66	  group co-owns every deployable path (owner decision OD9, layer 3). The cost: GitHub accepts an
67	  approval from any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days that group could approve another
68	  domain's PR. Domain review on normal days becomes a process rule with a monthly check, not a
69	  technical control. Because on-call approvers only
70	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
71	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
72	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
73	  approver, like L2, but that approver must own the path, and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
74	  the prod preview (OD2, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
75	  for speed.
76	- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
77	  business associate, as the brief implies.
78	
79	**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):
80	
81	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
82	   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
83	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
84	3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
85	4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.
86	
87	### Roles
88	
89	| Role | Rule |
90	|---|---|
91	| Author (engineer + their agent) | Never approves own change; GitHub blocks PR authors from approving (📖 R3.3.1). |
92	| Approver | Always an engineer, never an agent (owner rule, OD5). Named in CODEOWNERS; ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3); for an app-opened PR, ≠ the person who triggered it (⚠️ R3.3.4, layer 5). |
93	| Incident responder | Engineer who diagnoses and writes the fix or the JIT request. Never the on-call approver of the same shift (OD7). |
94	| On-call approver | Engineer on the on-call schedule, primary + backup, 24/7; wait ≤ 15 min (S7). While on call they only approve: they write no fix and file no JIT request, so the approver is always distinct from the author (OD7). The primary approves; the backup replaces an unavailable primary (OD2). No platform-team membership is required; all engineers follow one agreed approval procedure (OD2). |
95	| Data owner [design] | Named per tenant; co-approves real-data reads (layer 6). |
96	| Control owner | DevSecOps (1–2 people, GĐ-1); owns policies and metrics; not the only approver. |
97	
98	---
99	
100	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
101	
102	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
103	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
104	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
105	
106	**On Papaya's stack**
107	
108	- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
109	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
110	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
111	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
112	  holds.
113	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
114	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
115	    accepted as a process control, D2);
116	  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles (D2; `--restricted` per D3,
117	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
118	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
119	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.
120	    GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
121	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
122	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list
123	    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
124	    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
125	- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
126	  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
127	    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Until a service's logs are redacted at source
128	    (layer 6), it gets that service's metrics only. Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
129	    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
130	    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
131	    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
132	  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
133	  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
134	    TEAM sample (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b) or a small home-built flow (⚠️ R2.4.2) on the documented APIs
135	    `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2);
136	  - no standing prod-write permission set.
137	- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
138	  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
139	    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
140	    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
141	  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
142	    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
143	    JIT roles. This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
144	    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (key 📖 R4.4.5; need ⚠️ R4.6 #3);
145	  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:UserId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
146	  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
147	    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path).
148	- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
149	  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
150	- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`
151	  environment of the monorepo, in its `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4; immutable format assumed,
152	  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
153	- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
154	  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
155	- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
156	  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
157	  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so
158	  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).
159	
160	**Audit evidence.** Identity Center assignment export (S1); CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` /
161	`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
162	and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs
163	(📖 R2.8.1); quarterly access review of permission sets and GitHub admins.
164	
165	**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write and keep a free non-prod loop. Prod reads stay
166	fast for metrics and metadata, but shrink during the transition: because the engineer's access is the
167	agent's access, from phase 1 the engineer too loses raw logs and configuration of services not yet
168	redacted or moved to runtime secrets. Configuration values come from the IaC code instead (layer 1
169	above); raw logs that may hold customer data need an L3-data grant. The data owner is not on the
170	on-call schedule, so at night the grant is approved by the on-call approver alone and the data owner
171	reviews it the next working day [design]; the wait still counts against S7. This is
172	the largest cost of the first months. Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## Layer 2 — Agent runtime controls
177	
178	**Principle.** Agent-side controls are hygiene, not the boundary. They are central, versioned in git
179	and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
180	untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).
181	
182	**On Papaya's stack**
183	
184	- **Delivery:** server-managed settings (available on Team, 📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. With MDM, also
185	  an endpoint file; by default one managed source supplies most keys, so the two must carry the same
186	  keys or use `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.4). MDM is unknown; both are prepared.
187	- **Baseline** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4). All keys 📖 at the row cited:
188	
189	  | Key | Value and reason |
190	  |---|---|
191	  | `permissions.defaultMode` | `default` (Manual). A default, not a lock: users can switch to auto; VS Code remembers the last pick (D1, R6.9.3). |
192	  | `permissions.allow` | Read-only commands Papaya uses, to cut prompts (R6.9.3). |
193	  | `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` | `true`, one rule set (D1, research 6.9.4 Q4; R1.2.5). Cost: project and user rules are ignored, so the managed set must carry every deny/ask rule projects need; prompts likely rise (⚠️ research 6.9.4 Q4). |
194	  | `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode` | `"disable"`: removes bypass mode (P3a; R1.2.2). Auto mode, where a classifier approves instead of a person, stays available (D1) and is measured through `permission_mode`. |
195	  | `permissions.deny` / `ask` | Deny credential paths (R5.5.4; `Read(...)` syntax ⚠️ R1.8 #5). Ask for `WebFetch`, which the sandbox domain list does not limit (R1.6.2); cost: a prompt per fetch. The HIPAA template denies WebFetch (R5.5.4); "ask" is a deliberate deviation so that documentation lookups still work. |
196	  | `requiredMinimumVersion` | ≥ 2.1.285 for `allowedProviders` (R1.1.15), which also covers `--restricted` (2.1.248, R6.9.1b) and the plugin-pin fix (2.1.179, R6.2.7); ≥ 2.1.295 if any managed hook uses `onFailure: "block"` (R1.5.2); and ≥ the latest fixed advisory at rollout (R6.3.9). It does not end running sessions and fails open on a bad value (R1.1.13). |
197	  | `allowedProviders` + `forceLoginOrgUUID` | `["anthropic"]` + Papaya's org; closes most bypasses on **endpoint-managed** machines (R1.1.15). `forceLoginOrgUUID` checks claude.ai sign-ins only, not Claude Console sign-ins (R5.5.5); with it set, sessions on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `apiKeyHelper` are refused (R1.11.3.11). |
198	  | `allowManagedHooksOnly` | `true` (R1.5.4). |
199	  | sandbox | `sandbox.enabled`, `failIfUnavailable`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: false`, narrow `network.allowedDomains` locked by `network.allowManagedDomainsOnly`; `credentials` / `filesystem.denyRead` on `~/.aws`, which the sandbox can otherwise read (R1.6.3, R1.6.4). |
200	  | `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` | Left at its default `true`: sandboxed Bash runs without a prompt, so in Manual mode prompts are for edits, unsandboxed commands and fetches, not every command (R5.5.5b). A deliberate choice: the sandbox (no `~/.aws`, allowlisted network) is the control for those commands. The HIPAA README says to set `false` if policy needs a person to approve each command (R5.5.5b); cost of `false`: a prompt per command. |
201	  | MCP, plugins | Layer 4. |
202	  | OTel | Exporter on, content flags `0` (R1.1.20, R5.5.4). |
203	
204	- **Trade-off on AWS credentials [design].** With `~/.aws` hidden from the sandbox, the plan is to
205	  list `aws`, `pulumi` and `serverless` in `sandbox.excludedCommands`. Excluded commands run "with
206	  full access" (📖 R1.6.4), which likely includes the network (⚠️ inference). How the list matches
207	  commands (prefix or text, and chained commands) is not researched (⚠️). This is worse than an
208	  egress channel: `pulumi preview` runs the Pulumi program and `serverless` loads its config and
209	  plugins, all code in the repo that the agent can edit, so excluding them lets repo code run
210	  outside the sandbox with network access and with `~/.aws` readable (⚠️ inference). For these
211	  commands the sandbox gives no protection. And an injected `aws` command could send out the SSO
212	  token cache itself. That token likely opens every role assigned to the engineer for the rest of the
213	  portal session (📖 R2.1.5; token reuse ⚠️ R2.2.2), probably including JIT or data-read grants added
214	  later in that session (⚠️ inference). Mitigations [design]: a short portal session (📖 R2.1.5); end
215	  the existing portal session and sign in fresh **before** a JIT or data-read grant is created
216	  (whether ending a session invalidates a token already stolen is unverified ⚠️; ending it does not
217	  end role sessions, 📖 R2.4.3); an SCP that denies writes to resources outside Papaya's organization using
218	  `aws:ResourceOrgID` (key 📖 R2.3.8), on every OU, since the token can be stolen from a non-prod
219	  session; legitimate writes to outside resources need exceptions (⚠️ not inventoried). That SCP only stops Papaya's own credentials writing to a
220	  foreign bucket; it does not stop a command that sends the token to a non-AWS endpoint or uses the
221	  attacker's credentials (⚠️ inference). Prefer running `pulumi` and `serverless` against real
222	  accounts only in CI; on laptops keep them to non-prod roles, and move them into the phase-3
223	  container. Residual risk: token theft during a session. It is accepted
224	  because the engineer holds no **standing** prod write and no **standing** PHI read; during a JIT
225	  or data-read window the protection is the process rule in layer 1 (D2). Stronger option, phase 3:
226	  a separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions
227	  (⚠️ R6.5 #2).
228	- **Session types:**
229	
230	  | Session | Identity | Flags | Enforcement |
231	  |---|---|---|---|
232	  | Daily development (laptop) | non-prod roles + `ProdReadMetadata` | baseline | Auto mode by choice (D1); `--restricted` recommended (D3). |
233	  | Incident analysis (laptop) | meant to be `ProdReadMetadata` only | `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"`, started in an empty scratch directory, not the repo [design] | Process rule (D3, research 6.9.4 Q1–Q2). No WebFetch, and file tools confined to the working directory (📖 R6.9.1b); Edit/Write are excluded only if `--tools` acts as an exclusive list (⚠️ unverified), but Bash can still write in its working directory (📖 R1.6.3) and call any role in the cache. |
234	  | CI agent (hosted runner) | own GitHub App token; never `production` | `--restricted`, explicit `--tools`; all rules in a managed-settings file on the runner | Workflow file under CODEOWNERS (D3, research 6.9.4 Q5). The file is advisory if `Bash` is in `--tools` (layer 5). |
235	  | JIT terminal | JIT grant | no agent | Process rule (D2). |
236	  | Auto-mode environment (phase 3) | non-prod only | auto encouraged | D1 option (c). |
237	
238	- **Hard limits:** Bash rules are not a boundary (📖 R1.2.6); hooks fail open unless
239	  `"onFailure": "block"` (📖 R1.5.2); `--restricted` cannot be forced by a setting (📖 R6.9.1), and a `PATH` wrapper on laptops can be bypassed (⚠️ R6.9.1c);
240	  on laptops **without MDM**, a different login, an API key or a `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` variable skips
241	  server-managed settings, `allowedProviders` included (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ R1.8 #3, G11). So S5's
242	  "nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed" is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
243	- **Auto memory:** engineers review it and delete it after a suspicious session; residual risk with a
244	  named owner (D3).
245	- **Fallback:** switch to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers auto mode, a serious
246	  advisory appears, or an audit finds auto mode touched a protected scope (D1).
247	
248	**Audit evidence.** Managed settings in git with PR approvals; `/status` and `claude doctor` from
249	sampled machines (📖 R1.1.18); OTel `claude_code.tool_decision` (`permission_mode`) and
250	`claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user` (`duration_ms`, rubber-stamping signal) (fields 📖 research 6.6
251	D1 metrics; thresholds ⚠️). Settings-change audit events on Team: unknown (⚠️ R1.1.12).
252	
253	**Cost / value.** More prompts than auto mode, partly offset by the read-only allowlist. Compliance
254	gets one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices (P3c).

258	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
259	
260	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
261	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
262	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
263	no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
264	unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
265	many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
266	second approval by an owner of the same stack, who may be the first approver, so still two people
267	(OD8). Two edge cases: a PR that touches
268	paths of several owner teams needs an approval from each, which stays two people only if one
269	approver belongs to all those teams (otherwise it is a deviation from "two people" that the owner
270	should confirm, or the PR is split); a real-data read is not a change and has its own rule,
271	L3-data. Incidents use the same
272	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
273	
274	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
275	|---|---|---|---|---|
276	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
277	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
278	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
279	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, stacks that hold only IAM/SCP): the L3 owner team. L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver, who co-owns every path (OD9) | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
280	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); as a co-owner of every path (OD9), they own the service | layer 7 |
281	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9 | layer 6 |
282	
283	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
284	the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
285	owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
286	What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned by a designated L3 owner team
287	through a path-based rule (📖 R3.2.4), L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the
288	risk stop. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files, so they are approved by
289	the stack's owners, not the L3 team (OD8); automated checks make up for this: IAM Access Analyzer
290	`check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and the Pulumi policy pack (📖 R4.2.2). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need the L3 owner team, not
291	the domain team that edits it most.
292	
293	**On Papaya's stack**
294	
295	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
296	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
297	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
298	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
299	  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
300	- **L3 approvals [design]:** a path-based rule requires 1 approval from the team that owns each L3
301	  path (📖 R3.2.4); GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5) adds what
302	  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
303	  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3).
304	- **Who approves at night (OD9):** a fixed GitHub team, the on-call approvers, is listed as
305	  co-owner on every deployable path in CODEOWNERS, L3 paths included, next to the domain or L3
306	  team. One primary and one backup from that team are on call; any of them can approve any path.
307	  Membership changes only through a CODEOWNERS/team PR, not per shift. Cost: an approval from any
308	  listed owner satisfies code-owner review (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days a member could approve
309	  another domain's PR. Mitigation [design]: process rule "outside your shift, approve only your own
310	  domain", and a monthly report of approvals by group members outside their shifts and outside their
311	  domain (layer 7). Whether Papaya's team size allows full coverage is unknown
312	  (§1, S7).
313	- **Risk stop [design]:** applies to every deploy, whatever the level. The deploy job previews prod;
314	  on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change, a network or security-group change, or an advisory
315	  policy finding it stops and posts the filtered preview. An engineer opens a second PR that adds
316	  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` (`<sha>` = the stopped commit) holding that SHA and the
317	  preview hash; the workflow does not open it, because the setting that lets Actions create and approve PRs stays
318	  off (📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3). CODEOWNERS on `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` names the owners of that stack and the
319	  on-call group (OD8, OD9). The approver is ≠ author and may be the first PR's approver, who now sees
320	  the prod diff. Merging it triggers the deploy on the new HEAD, which previews again and continues
321	  only if the hash matches the approved one; if another PR merged in between, the hash differs and
322	  the deploy stops again (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). Cost: while a stack is
323	  stopped, later merges to that stack stop too until a matching approval lands. A
324	  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
325	  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
326	  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
327	- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
328	  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
329	  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
330	  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
331	- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
332	  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
333	  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
334	  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
335	  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
336	- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
337	  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
338	  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
339	  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
340	- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
341	  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
342	- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
343	  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1).
344	- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
345	  slow unrelated tests skipped [design].
346	
347	**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)
348	
349	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
350	unavailable).
351	
352	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
353	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
354	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
355	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
356	3. R, a co-owner of `serverless.yml` through the on-call group (OD9), reviews the diff. If R
357	   catches a missing queue change, R does not fix it (OD7): E pushes the fix, the stale approval is
358	   dismissed, and R approves again, one more review round (Options §6). E merges.
359	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
360	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.
361	
362	**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
363	retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.
364	
365	**Cost / value.** One approver for every prod change, from the owners of the path; two approvals
366	(same or another owner) when the risk stop fires; more than one approver only for a PR across
367	several owner teams. None in non-prod.
368	Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

409	## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening
410	
411	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
412	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
413	checks as human code (S10).
414	
415	**On Papaya's stack**
416	
417	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
418	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
419	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
420	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
421	  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
422	  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
423	  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
424	  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
425	    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
426	    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
427	    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
428	    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
429	  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
430	    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
431	    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). Self-hosted runners "can be persistently
432	    compromised by untrusted code" from anyone who can open a PR, and runner groups limit only which
433	    repositories use them (📖 R3.5.2); in a monorepo any workflow can target the runner's label.
434	    How to restrict a runner to one workflow is not researched (⚠️ G15); just-in-time runners exist
435	    (📖 R3.5.2, not read in detail). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
436	    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
437	  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
438	  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register;
439	  - optionally a separate environment (e.g. `production-k0s`), limited to `main` and referenced
440	    only by the k0s/Firebase deploy workflow, so AWS deploy jobs cannot read these secrets
441	    [design].
442	
443	  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
444	  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
445	  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
446	  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
447	  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
448	- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
449	  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
450	- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
451	  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA"; the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
452	  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5; conclusion [design]).
453	- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
454	  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5); CI validates the file, because
455	  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).
456	- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,

458	- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
459	  requests (📖 R1.7.8); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);

481	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
482	
483	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
484	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
485	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
486	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
487	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
488	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
489	
490	**On Papaya's stack**
491	
492	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
493	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role from
494	    phase 1 (existing broad read roles are removed) and the SCP from phase 2
495	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
496	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
497	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
498	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
499	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
500	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
501	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
502	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
503	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
504	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
505	    redacted summary. This
506	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
507	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
508	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
509	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
510	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
511	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
512	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
513	  1.11.4 L6).
514	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default (sandboxed Bash runs without a prompt, layer 2); the auto-mode
515	  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions and 5.7 % of 1,000 synthetic exfiltration
516	  attempts (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path
517	  (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no WebFetch, likely no edit tools (layer 2), and runs outside
518	  the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
519	  commands (layer 2), including the SSO token cache; "no standing write, no PHI read" limits what
520	  the token opens, except during a JIT or data-read window (layer 2 mitigations). Shared knowledge
521	  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is exempt from the protected-path rules unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
522	- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
523	  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
524	  (GĐ-3, unconfirmed).
525	- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
526	  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14: until cleaned, non-prod follows the GĐ-9 data-read rule). Cost: until scanned, that store is
527	  not part of the free loop.
528	- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
529	  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
530	- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a

545	## Layer 7 — Observability, audit, incident response and break-glass
546	
547	**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
548	named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
549	is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.
550	
551	**On Papaya's stack**
552	
553	- **Audit stores:**
554	  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
555	    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
556	    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (cost 📖 R2.6.3; selection
557	    ⚠️ R2.9 #5), which makes the archive
558	    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
559	  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
560	  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
561	    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
562	    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
563	    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
564	    with an expected copy (G8);
565	  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
566	    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
567	  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
568	- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
569	  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
570	  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
571	  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
572	- **Drift [design]:** its own role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
573	  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
574	  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
575	  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
576	  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
577	  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
578	  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
579	  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
580	  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
581	  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
582	- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7), as
583	  decided in framing round 1, and, because of OD7, a minimal incident-responder schedule; the
584	  latter extends that decision. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
585	  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
586	  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
587	  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5).
588	- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:
589	
590	  | Step | Rule |
591	  |---|---|
592	  | When | The PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. |
593	  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
594	  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (Options §4b; OD7; backup rule OD2). |
595	  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). |
596	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
597	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
598	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
599	
600	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
601	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
602	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
603	
604	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
605	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
606	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
607	  this draft). On a breach,
608	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
609	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
610	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
611	  (D2, ⚠️).
612	
613	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail; exported GitHub audit log; change records and monthly
614	reconciliation (S3, S8 ≤ 30 min); JIT requests, reconciliations, codify PRs; drift tickets; on-call
615	schedule and approval waits (S7); monthly report of approvals by on-call group members outside
616	their shift and domain (OD9).
617	
618	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
619	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
620	incidents, plus detection.

627	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
628	attacks.

29	## 1. The decision in one page
30	
31	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
32	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
33	
34	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
35	
36	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
37	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
38	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
39	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
40	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
41	
42	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
43	|---|---|
44	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
45	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, OD1, OD6; storage conditions [design], layer 5). |
46	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
47	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
48	
49	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
50	
51	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
52	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
53	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
54	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
55	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
56	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an owner of the stack approves the prod preview [design].
57	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
58	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
59	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
60	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
61	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
62	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
63	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
64	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** code-owner review means an approver must own the file,
65	  at L2 as at L3. So that one on-call primary can approve any path at 2 a.m., the on-call approver
66	  group co-owns every deployable path (owner decision OD9, layer 3). The cost: GitHub accepts an
67	  approval from any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days that group could approve another
68	  domain's PR. Domain review on normal days becomes a process rule with a monthly check, not a
69	  technical control. Because on-call approvers only
70	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
71	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
72	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
73	  approver, like L2, but that approver must own the path, and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
74	  the prod preview (OD2, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
75	  for speed.
76	- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
77	  business associate, as the brief implies.
78	
79	**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):
80	
81	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
82	   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
83	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
84	3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
85	4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.

100	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
101	
102	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
103	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
104	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
105	
106	**On Papaya's stack**
107	
108	- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
109	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
110	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
111	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
112	  holds.
113	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
114	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
115	    accepted as a process control, D2);
116	  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles (D2; `--restricted` per D3,
117	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
118	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
119	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.
120	    GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
121	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
122	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list
123	    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
124	    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
125	- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
126	  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
127	    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Until a service's logs are redacted at source
128	    (layer 6), it gets that service's metrics only. Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
129	    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
130	    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
131	    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
132	  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
133	  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
134	    TEAM sample (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b) or a small home-built flow (⚠️ R2.4.2) on the documented APIs
135	    `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2);
136	  - no standing prod-write permission set.
137	- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
138	  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
139	    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
140	    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
141	  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
142	    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
143	    JIT roles. This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
144	    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (key 📖 R4.4.5; need ⚠️ R4.6 #3);
145	  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:UserId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
146	  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
147	    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path).
148	- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
149	  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
150	- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`

152	  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
153	- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
154	  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
155	- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
156	  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
157	  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so

161	`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
162	and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs

165	**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write and keep a free non-prod loop. Prod reads stay

167	agent's access, from phase 1 the engineer too loses raw logs and configuration of services not yet
168	redacted or moved to runtime secrets. Configuration values come from the IaC code instead (layer 1
169	above); raw logs that may hold customer data need an L3-data grant. The data owner is not on the
170	on-call schedule, so at night the grant is approved by the on-call approver alone and the data owner
171	reviews it the next working day [design]; the wait still counts against S7. This is
172	the largest cost of the first months. Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.

258	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
259	
260	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
261	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
262	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
263	no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
264	unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
265	many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
266	second approval by an owner of the same stack, who may be the first approver, so still two people
267	(OD8). Two edge cases: a PR that touches
268	paths of several owner teams needs an approval from each, which stays two people only if one
269	approver belongs to all those teams (otherwise it is a deviation from "two people" that the owner
270	should confirm, or the PR is split); a real-data read is not a change and has its own rule,
271	L3-data. Incidents use the same
272	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
273	
274	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
275	|---|---|---|---|---|
276	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
277	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
278	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
279	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, stacks that hold only IAM/SCP): the L3 owner team. L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver, who co-owns every path (OD9) | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
280	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); as a co-owner of every path (OD9), they own the service | layer 7 |
281	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9 | layer 6 |
282	
283	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
284	the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
285	owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
286	What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned by a designated L3 owner team
287	through a path-based rule (📖 R3.2.4), L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the
288	risk stop. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files, so they are approved by
289	the stack's owners, not the L3 team (OD8); automated checks make up for this: IAM Access Analyzer
290	`check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and the Pulumi policy pack (📖 R4.2.2). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need the L3 owner team, not
291	the domain team that edits it most.
292	
293	**On Papaya's stack**
294	
295	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
296	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
297	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
298	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
299	  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
300	- **L3 approvals [design]:** a path-based rule requires 1 approval from the team that owns each L3
301	  path (📖 R3.2.4); GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5) adds what
302	  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
303	  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3).
304	- **Who approves at night (OD9):** a fixed GitHub team, the on-call approvers, is listed as
305	  co-owner on every deployable path in CODEOWNERS, L3 paths included, next to the domain or L3
306	  team. One primary and one backup from that team are on call; any of them can approve any path.
307	  Membership changes only through a CODEOWNERS/team PR, not per shift. Cost: an approval from any
308	  listed owner satisfies code-owner review (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days a member could approve
309	  another domain's PR. Mitigation [design]: process rule "outside your shift, approve only your own
310	  domain", and a monthly report of approvals by group members outside their shifts and outside their
311	  domain (layer 7). Whether Papaya's team size allows full coverage is unknown
312	  (§1, S7).
313	- **Risk stop [design]:** applies to every deploy, whatever the level. The deploy job previews prod;
314	  on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change, a network or security-group change, or an advisory
315	  policy finding it stops and posts the filtered preview. An engineer opens a second PR that adds
316	  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` (`<sha>` = the stopped commit) holding that SHA and the
317	  preview hash; the workflow does not open it, because the setting that lets Actions create and approve PRs stays
318	  off (📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3). CODEOWNERS on `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` names the owners of that stack and the
319	  on-call group (OD8, OD9). The approver is ≠ author and may be the first PR's approver, who now sees
320	  the prod diff. Merging it triggers the deploy on the new HEAD, which previews again and continues
321	  only if the hash matches the approved one; if another PR merged in between, the hash differs and
322	  the deploy stops again (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). Cost: while a stack is
323	  stopped, later merges to that stack stop too until a matching approval lands. A
324	  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
325	  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
326	  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
327	- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
328	  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
329	  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
330	  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
331	- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
332	  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
333	  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
334	  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
335	  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
336	- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
337	  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
338	  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
339	  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
340	- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
341	  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
342	- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
343	  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1).
344	- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
345	  slow unrelated tests skipped [design].
346	
347	**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)
348	
349	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
350	unavailable).
351	
352	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
353	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
354	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
355	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
356	3. R, a co-owner of `serverless.yml` through the on-call group (OD9), reviews the diff. If R
357	   catches a missing queue change, R does not fix it (OD7): E pushes the fix, the stale approval is
358	   dismissed, and R approves again, one more review round (Options §6). E merges.
359	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
360	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.
361	
362	**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
363	retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.
364	
365	**Cost / value.** One approver for every prod change, from the owners of the path; two approvals
366	(same or another owner) when the risk stop fires; more than one approver only for a PR across
367	several owner teams. None in non-prod.
368	Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

409	## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening
410	
411	**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
412	least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
413	checks as human code (S10).
414	
415	**On Papaya's stack**
416	
417	- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
418	  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
419	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
420	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
421	  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
422	  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
423	  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
424	  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
425	    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
426	    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
427	    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
428	    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
429	  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
430	    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
431	    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). Self-hosted runners "can be persistently
432	    compromised by untrusted code" from anyone who can open a PR, and runner groups limit only which
433	    repositories use them (📖 R3.5.2); in a monorepo any workflow can target the runner's label.
434	    How to restrict a runner to one workflow is not researched (⚠️ G15); just-in-time runners exist
435	    (📖 R3.5.2, not read in detail). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
436	    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
437	  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
438	  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register;
439	  - optionally a separate environment (e.g. `production-k0s`), limited to `main` and referenced
440	    only by the k0s/Firebase deploy workflow, so AWS deploy jobs cannot read these secrets
441	    [design].
442	
443	  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
444	  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
445	  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
446	  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
447	  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
448	- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
449	  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
450	- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
451	  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA"; the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
452	  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5; conclusion [design]).
453	- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
454	  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5); CI validates the file, because
455	  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).
456	- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
457	  📖 R3.5.4).
458	- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
459	  requests (📖 R1.7.8); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);
460	  `--restricted` and explicit `--tools` (D3; passing it through `claude_args` unverified, ⚠️ research
461	  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
462	  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
463	  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),
464	  so with `Bash` in `--tools` the runner file is advisory (⚠️ R3.5.1, R3.6 #4).
465	- **App-opened PRs:** a required check with a pinned source app confirms at least one approval by a
466	  human who did not trigger the run; counting approvals is not enough, since the app's own approval
467	  might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3; 📖 R3.2.5).
468	- **Required checks (S10):** secret scanning, dependency check, SAST (products: G4); IAM Access

471	**Audit evidence.** Workflows and lockfile in git; audit-log events such as

481	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
482	
483	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
484	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
485	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
486	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
487	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
488	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
489	
490	**On Papaya's stack**
491	
492	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
493	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role from
494	    phase 1 (existing broad read roles are removed) and the SCP from phase 2
495	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
496	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
497	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
498	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
499	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
500	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
501	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
502	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
503	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
504	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
505	    redacted summary. This
506	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
507	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
508	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
509	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
510	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
511	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
512	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
513	  1.11.4 L6).
514	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default (sandboxed Bash runs without a prompt, layer 2); the auto-mode
515	  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions and 5.7 % of 1,000 synthetic exfiltration
516	  attempts (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path
517	  (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no WebFetch, likely no edit tools (layer 2), and runs outside
518	  the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
519	  commands (layer 2), including the SSO token cache; "no standing write, no PHI read" limits what
520	  the token opens, except during a JIT or data-read window (layer 2 mitigations). Shared knowledge
521	  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is exempt from the protected-path rules unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
522	- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
523	  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
524	  (GĐ-3, unconfirmed).
525	- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
526	  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14: until cleaned, non-prod follows the GĐ-9 data-read rule). Cost: until scanned, that store is
527	  not part of the free loop.
528	- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
529	  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
530	- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
531	  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
532	  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).
533	
534	**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data (📖 R5.4.3; ⚠️ R5.7 #5);
535	data-read requests and the data-read role's CloudTrail; planted-injection reports (layer 8); non-prod
536	scan results (S11).
537	
538	**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
539	Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2;
540	actions ⚠️ G13) and by process
541	elsewhere, and a record per exception (S9).
